name: Valencia Central Station
title: Valencia Central Station
overview:
The brief for Valencia Central Station reimagines the below-ground railway station by opening up the platforms to natural light, fresh air and views, while creating a stronger connection between the station and the city above.

The platforms are arranged across two levels, with access bridges, escalators and circulation routes bringing daylight deep into the station. Visual connections between the different levels make movement through the station clear and intuitive.

At ground level, a lightweight modular canopy follows the geometry of the surrounding landscape, providing a contemporary interpretation of the 19th-century railway canopy of the historic Valencia Nord station opposite.

Placing the railway tracks below ground removes a barrier that has divided this part of Valencia for the best part of a century, allowing the city to reconnect across the former railway corridor. Central Park can extend north towards Valencia Nord and City Hall Square, creating a continuous ribbon of planting, pedestrian routes and cycle paths. Through its linear form and integration with the landscape, the new station becomes part of this sequence rather than an interruption to it.

Between the new station and Valencia Nord, a new Station Square brings the two buildings together within a shared public space. The square reinforces the presence of the much-loved historic station within the neighbourhood, while allowing the new architecture to establish its own distinct identity.

Below ground, the existing terminus is transformed into a through station, creating a new cross-city connection that links with the Litoral route running north–south, parallel to the coast. The station adopts a kit-of-parts approach to construction, using prefabrication to reduce construction time and associated disruption, minimise waste and support whole-life carbon reduction. Together, architecture, infrastructure and landscape form an integrated station that reconnects Valencia and strengthens the relationship between the railway and the city.
